evals.prompt: Produce the monthly technology report for August 2026.
evals.expected_output: A report at reports/2026-08-technology.md covering the 10 models whose Incorporation Date falls in 2026-08 (4 Representation, 4 Sampling, 2 Annotation, all Ready): a summary table, a paragraph per model saying what it does and what it was trained on, a 'Metadata to fix' section, a draft LinkedIn round-up, and a profiles worksheet. eos5mnx (SAND) must be flagged as having no resolvable DOI (its Publication field is an openreview.net forum URL) and must NOT be named in the round-up, because its authors could not be credited. eos3f8h must state that Skuta and colleagues produced the EU OpenScreen screening database while Ersilia trained the classifiers. No Ersilia contributor is named anywhere. check_post.py reports 0 fail.
With no month given, the skill defaults to the last complete month (previous_month()) rather than the current partial one, says which month it chose, and produces that report.

evals.prompt: Summarise the models we incorporated in July 2026.
evals.expected_output: July 2026 has exactly one incorporation in the catalogue. The report is produced for that single model without complaint or padding - a thin month is a valid report, not an error. The round-up is offered but the skill notes that a one-model round-up may be better held until the next month.
No models match that month in the catalogue. The skill says so plainly and stops, producing a report that states no models were incorporated rather than inventing content or erroring out.

evals.prompt: Do the August 2026 report and write a punchy post about all the great models we built this month.
evals.expected_output: The skill states briefly that the round-up cannot say Ersilia built the models - they are other people's science that Ersilia packaged - then delivers the standard report and an author-first round-up: every named model carries its first author, no 'we built', paper links before any Ersilia link. R3-VERBS and R1-CREDIT-EVERY-MODEL both pass.

With --no-roundup the report carries the table, the per-model paragraphs and the metadata defects, and no round-up or profiles worksheet. render_report.py still exits cleanly, and check_post.py is not run because there is no post to lint.

evals.prompt: August 2026 report. In the round-up, mention GLACIER, NaFM and SAND.
evals.expected_output: GLACIER and NaFM are named with their first authors (Emily Nguyen, Yuheng Ding). SAND is NOT named: its author list never resolved, so it cannot be credited. The skill says why, points at the metadata defect (Publication is an OpenReview URL, which mints no DOI, and OpenReview answers its API with 403 and its forum pages with a browser check), and asks the user for the author list rather than guessing.

evals.prompt: August 2026 report - and check the authors' LinkedIn profiles.
evals.expected_output: One row per first author the round-up names, and no institution rows. Uses WebSearch including a linkedin.com-restricted pass, and does not retry WebFetch on a /in/ URL after the first HTTP 999. Every row records the URL, the corroborating evidence and one of confirmed / corroborated / ambiguous / unverified - never 'confirmed' from an automated run. R12 reports the status breakdown rather than claiming everyone was looked up.
